svg.title: The web-search chain: a selected provider, then the keyless hops, with the provider named in the digest
svg.desc: The search chain starts at the selected provider. Under the auto fallback policy it may move to the keyless ddgs metasearch and then to the keyless DuckDuckGo page hop. A named provider is strict. Every search key uses the same rotation engine as a model key, and the rich digest names the provider that ultimately produced the results.

g.text: The fallback policy decides how far the chain may move
auto: selected → ddgs → legacy · none: selected only · ddgs: selected → ddgs · legacy: selected → ddgs → legacy
An explicit provider is strict: missing credentials or an upstream failure are surfaced, not silently swapped.
with no keys set, auto falls back to the two
keyless hops, so search works out of the box
the digest names the provider that answered;
every key try is a row in web-search analytics
Context7 is never picked by auto: it answers with library documentation rather than web pages.
Web fetch extracts the page's main content as markdown with a 24,000-character cap and names the extracted total.
